Name: George Washington
fact: This president's teeth were not made of wood, but rather was a combination of human teeth, cow teeth, elephant and hippo ivory, brass, and gold.
DefE: The Constitution took effect in 1789, reaching the required nine of thirteen states approving of it. It marked the transition from a weaker confederation to a stronger central government.
DefM: (1794) Agreement between U.S. and Great Britain to stop a new war; it also was agreed upon to resolve unresolved grievances of 1783 Treaty of Paris. This all happened after seizure of American merchant ships that were trading with France by British navy.

Name: John Adams
fact: This president and his son are the first father-son president duo.
DefE: (1797-1798) a diplomatic scandal where French agents demanded bribes from American envoys to start peace talks; started an undeclared naval war between U.S. and France.
DefM: (1798) acts passed by Federalist congress aimed to suppress political power of immigrants, as well as silence critics from Democratic-Republican Party; led to the argument by Thomas Jefferson and James Madison through the Kentucky and Virginia Resolutions that introduced the idea of nullification, where states could declare unconstitutional federal laws as "void."

Name: Thomas Jefferson
fact: Due to this president's great writing abilities and poor public speaking abilities, he established a precedent of sending written messages to Congress.
DefE: (1803) land deal between the United States and France where the U.S. bought 828,000 square miles of land west of the Mississippi River for $15 million.
DefM: (1803) the first case in which the Supreme Court of the United States invalidated a law passed by Congress.

Name: James Madison
fact: In addition to being president, he also helped write The Federalist Papers to persuade New York to ratify the U.S. Constitution. These papers argued for a stronger federal government.
DefE: (1814-1815) secret series of meetings held by New England Federalists from December 15, 1814, to January 5, 1815, in Hartford, Connecticut, to protest the War of 1812 and the political power of Southern states; backlash contributed to the final collapse of the Federalist party.
DefM: (1809) an act passed to replace the failed Embargo Act by reopening trade with all foreign nations except France and Britain.

Name: James Monroe
fact: This president supported the American Colonization Society (ACS), which seeked to support the migration of free African-Americans to Africa, namely Liberia.
DefE: (1823) Foreign policy declaration by James Monroe; stated that Western Hemisphere was closed to European colonization and intervention.
DefM: (1820) The compromise balanced free and slave states by admitting Missouri as a free state and Maine as a free state; banned slavery in Louisiana Purchase territory north of 36°30′. Was eventually overturned by the 1854 Kansas-Nebraska Act.

Name: John Quincy Adams
fact: This president is known for the Amistad case before the Supreme Court while serving as U.S. Congressman.
DefE: (1824) alleged political deal between Henry Clay and John Quincy Adams; Clay allegedly used his influence as Speaker of the House to secure Adams's presidency against Andrew Jackson; Clay was appointed Secretary of State.
DefM: (1819) U.S.-Spain agreement that gave Florida to the U.S. for $5 million. Went into effect in 1821. This was notable for the involvement of John Quincy Adams in negotiations.

Name: Andrew Jackson
fact: Though heavily influenced by Thomas Jefferson, Jefferson himself stated that this president was a "dangerous" man and was unfit for presidency.
DefE: (1830s) Andrew Jackson's political campaign to destroy the Second Bank of the United States; in 1832, he removed all federal deposits from the national bank and replaced them with state-chartered "pet banks." The collapse was encapsulated by the expiration of its charter in 1836, followed by the Panic of 1837.
DefM: (1833) Allowed the U.S. president to use military enforcement for federal tariff laws. Created during the Nullification Crisis after South Carolina declared tariffs (known as Tariff of Abominations) null and void and threatened to leave the Union.

Name: Martin Van Buren
fact: This president was nicknamed "Old Kinderhook" or "O.K.", which eventually morphed into the term "ok."
DefE: (1830s) a severe U.S. financial crisis and six-year economic depression that began when banks in New York City suspended hard-currency payments. Involved the shift from federal funds to unregulated state "pet banks."
DefM: (1830s) Forced Native American tribes living east of the Mississippi River to relocate to federal territory in the West. The pressure on tribes, including the Cherokee, Choctaw, Chickasaw, Creek, and Seminole nations, infamously led to Worcester v. Georgia and the Trail of Tears.

Name: William Henry Harrison
fact: This president and his grandson are the only grandfather-grandson pair in U.S. history.
DefE: (1811) Near Lafayette, Indiana, where U.S. troops battled Native American forces led by Tenskatawa. Led to 150-200 U.S. casualties, 130-200 Native American losses. Seen as a defeat for the Native American confederacy, brother of Tenskatawa and Shawnee Chief, Tecumseh, sought alliances with the British during the War of 1812.
DefM: NA

Name: John Tyler
fact: Even though this person was president during the 19th century, he is known for having a grandson who lived through the 21st century.
event: being kicked Out of Whig Party
DefE: (1841) Happened after this president vetoed bills to re-establish the national bank. This caused this president to be dubbed the "president without a party."
DefM: (1845) Texas joins the U.S. as the 28th state. Came after their 1836 independence from Mexico, though the U.S. feared starting war with Mexico and upsetting the balance of free and slave states. An initial annexation treaty was rejected, but a join resolution led to the state's ratification a year later.

Name: James K. Polk
fact: He is the only Speaker of the House to become president of the U.S.
DefE: (1840s) Mexico gives up 500,000 square miles of land to the U.S. during the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo, ending the Mexican-American War. Included all of parts of states, including California, Nevada, Utah, Arizona, New Mexico, Colorado, Wyoming, Oklahoma, Kansas, and Texas.
DefM: (1846s) Set international boundary between U.S. and British North America (Canada) at the 49th parallel west of the Rocky Mountains to the Pacific Ocean. Paved way for the Oregon Territory's creation, and helped the U.S. focus on the Mexican-American War.

Name: Zachary Taylor
fact: The party that this president ran for president as had nominated him without him knowing it, as he was away on military duty.
DefE: (1840s) a mass migration of roughly 300,000 "49ers" to California following the discovery of gold at Sutter's Mill

Name: Millard Fillmore
fact: This president was known for also running again under the "Know-Nothing" Party, a political party known for anti-immigrant and anti-Catholic (nativist) sentiment; this party was also known as the American Party.
DefE: Admitted California as a free state; Allowed decision of slavery in Utah/New Mexico to be based off popular sovereignty; Enacted a new and more extreme fugitive slave law; banned slave trade (but not slavery) in Washington D.C., and disputed Texas borders.
DefM: Part of Compromise of 1850; required all U.S. citizens to assist in capturing and returning escaped enslaved people.

Name: Franklin Pierce
fact: This president's administration is known for the Gadsden Purchase, which secured a strip of land in southern Arizona and New Mexico from Mexico for $10 million in order to secure a southern route for the Transcontinental Railroad.
DefE: (1854) Memo where U.S. diplomats conspired to have U.S. acquire/seize Cuba from Spain if Spain refused to sell it. An extension of Manifest Destiny as well as the continuation of tension between anti-slavery and pro-slavery groups.
DefM: (1854) Allowed for Kansas and Nebraska to decide policy of slavery by popular sovereignty; proposed by Stephen A. Douglas. Also repealed the Missouri Compromise of 1820, and caused a rush to both states in the form of warfare, referred to as "Bleeding Kansas."

Name: James Buchanan
fact: This president is widely considered to be the worst U.S. president, specifically due to his support of pro-Southern policies leading up to the Civil War (e.g., Lecompton Constitution), as well as his inaction during secession of the states.
event: John Brown's Raid at Harper's Ferry
DefE: (1859) Failed attempt to spark a slave rebellion in Harper's Ferry, Virginia. This terrified Southern slaveholders who feared for any slave revolts, while Northerners and abolitionists saw Brown as a martyr.
DefM: (1857) Declared African Americans as not citizens; Congress cannot ban slavery in territories.

Name: Abraham Lincoln
fact: He is the tallest U.S. president at 6 feet and 4 inches tall.
event: His assassination by John Wilkes Booth
DefE: (1865) This president was assassinated by Confederate sympathizer and actor John Wilkes Booth at Ford's Theatre in Washington D.C.; led to Andrew Johnson being sworn in.
DefM: (1863) Declaration that enslaved people in Confederate states were free. Specifically applied to the seceded states, as border states in Maryland and Kentucky were excluded to prevent further secession. Also shifted the Civil War from the war about preserving the Union to a crusade against slavery.

Name: Andrew Johnson
fact: In addition to being impeached, this president also saw the threat of being removed from office, but was acquitted by only one vote (short of the two-thirds majority).
event: His impeachment over Tenure of Office Act
act: Civil Rights Act of 1866 (after attempting to veto)
DefE: (1868) This president was impeached for violating the Tenure of Office Act (preventing the president from removing Senate-confirmed officeholders and cabinet members without Senate approval). This president was acquitted by a single vote and remained in office.
DefM: (1866) The first United States federal law to define citizenship and state that all citizens are equally protected by the law.

Name: Ulysses S. Grant
fact: This president coined the term "Unconditional Surrender", which meant that the defeated party yields without negotiation, guarantee, or concession.
DefE: (1869) In Utah, the Union Pacific and Central Pacific railroads finally meet, culminating the creation of the first Transcontinental Railroad after the Pacific Railway Act of 1862 passed. the Union Pacific heavily relied on Irish immigrant laborers, while the Central Pacific relied on Chinese immigrant laborers.
DefM: (1870) Prohibited federal and state governments from denying any citizen the right to vote based on "race, color, or previous condition of servitude." However, loopholes led to Southern states applying poll taxes, literacy tests, and grandfather clauses to essentially deny these rights.

Name: Rutherford B. Hayes
fact: This president was the first to have a telephone installed in the White House.
DefE: (1877) Disputed the 1876 U.S. Presidential Election and ended the Reconstruction Era. This person was named as president over Samuel J. Tilden following disputed votes in 3 states. The end of military Reconstruction led to the establishment of Jim Crow Laws in the South.
DefM: (1870s) System designed to disenfranchise African Americans under the idea of "separate but equal" established by Plessy v. Ferguson (1896). Included public segregation and voting restrictions, and is named after a 19th-century minstrel show character used by white performers in blackface.

Name: James A. Garfield
fact: As a political candidate, this president was a House Representative, Senator-elect, and President-elect at the same time.
event: His assassination over the civil service system
DefE: (1881) This president was shot in July of that year, and died in September of the same year. The assassin, Charles Guiteau, was a supporter of the "Stalwart" faction of Republicans, and apparently hoped that vice president Chester A. Arthur, a supporter of the spoils system, would become president. This president initially survived the gunshot wounds, but unhygenic medical practices led to infection, later killing him. This president's death also led to the 1883 Pendleton Act.
DefM: (1880s) Later accomplished by the Pendleton Act, sought to replace the spoils-based system with merit-based system for federal jobs.

Name: Chester A. Arthur
fact: Though he served as Collector of the Port of New York (meaning he benefitted from the civil service system), it became ironic due to the fact that he would pass the Pendleton Civil Service Act.
DefE: (1883) After 14 years of construction, the Brooklyn Bridge was opened. This marked a milestone in industrialization and urban growth during the Gilded Age.
DefM: (1882) Banned Chinese immigrant laborers from entering the United States; first major U.S. law to restrict immigration based on race and nationality, and demonstrated U.S. government action during a time of nativism and labor competition.

Name: Grover Cleveland
fact: In this president's first term, he managed to veto 414 bills, more than all the preceding presidents combined.
DefE: (1894) Nationwide railroad strike in the United States that paralyzed western rail traffic and marked a major turning point in federal intervention in labor disputes.
DefM: (1896)  Landmark Supreme Court case that established the "separate but equal" doctrine, legally upholding racial segregation and cementing Jim Crow laws until the 1960s.

Name: Benjamin Harrison
fact: This president added 6 states to the Union: Montana, Washington, South/North Dakota, Wyoming, and Idaho.
DefE: (1892) A violent labor conflict between the Amalgamated Association of Iron and Steel Workers and Carnegie Steel management at the Homestead plant in Pennsylvania.
DefM: Raised average import duties to nearly 50%, the highest protective rate in U.S. history at that point.

Name: William McKinley
fact: This president has a tariff (passed in the presidency just before) named after him.
DefE: (1901) This president was shot and killed in September by an anarchist. Led to Theodore Roosevelt becoming president, and the start of the transition from the Gilded Age to the Progressive Era with more government intervention.
DefM: (1901) U.S. provision forcing Cuba's constitution to limit Cuban sovereignty and make it an island under U.S. protectorate following the Spanish-American War. Bypassed the 1898 Teller Amendment promising the U.S. wouldn't annex Cuba (while also not annexing Cuba).

Name: Theodore Roosevelt
fact: This president asserted the "big stick" diplomacy, which meant negotiating peacefully while maintaining military and economic threat.
act: Meat Inspection Act / Pure Food and Drug Act
DefE: (1903) U.S. acquires and builds the Panama Canal by supporting a Panamanian revolt against Colombia in 1903, leading to the Hay-Bunau-Varilla Treaty.
DefM: (1906) Progressive Era consumer-protection laws motivated by muckraking journalism like The Jungle by Upton Sinclair. The first of the two prohibited sale of adulterated or misbranded livestock and meat products, and required sanitary standards for meatpacking plants. The second banned the manufacture, sale, or transportation of adulterated (impure/contaminated) or misbranded (falsely labeled) foods and patent medicines in interstate commerce.

Name: William Howard Taft
fact: He was fat. He also asserted "Dollar Diplomacy", which meant using American economic power through loans and private investments to expand international influence instead of using military force.
DefE: (1912) Emotional moment during the Election of 1912 where this president cried while his former mentor and best friend, Theodore Roosevelt, publicly attacked him.
DefM: (1909) Compromise tariff that failed to lower high protective tariff rates. This split the Republican Party and alienated the Progressive wing.

Name: Woodrow Wilson
fact: This president initially opposed women's suffrage, but eventually changed his stance to support the 19th amendment. Additionally, he asserted "Moral Diplomacy", prioritizing ethical principles over economic or strategic interests.
DefE: (1919) Ended WWI, forced Germany to accept full war blame and reparations, and created the League of Nations (though Congress would reject joining). The refusal to join reflected a theme of isolationism over the next decade for the U.S. German reparations would also be a motivator for the later growth of the Nazi party led by Adolf Hitler.
DefM: (1919/20) Operations by U.S. Attorney A. Mitchell Palmer and J. Edgar Hoover during the First Red Scare; followed the 1917 Bolshevik Revolution in Russia, and was also sparked by a 1919 wave of anarchist mail bombings. Targeted communists, socialists, anarchists, and radical labor union members.

Name: Warren G. Harding
fact: This president's campaign ran on the promise of "Return to Normalcy", which meant using the country's exposure to the Red Scare and censorship to win presidency.
act: Policies of the Washington Naval Conference
DefE: (1920s) A major political corruption event in the early 1920s involving Secretary of the Interior Albert B. Fall leasing federal oil reserves to private companies for bribes. Represented one of the pitfalls of this president's "Ohio Gang" during his presidency.
DefM: (1921-22) Sought to limit a post-WWI naval arms race, reduce tensions in the Pacific, and curb military spending through non-binding, unilateral diplomacy outside of the League of Nations.

Name: Calvin Coolidge
fact: This president's nickname indicates that he was quiet.
event: First use of radio during presidential speeches
DefE: (1920s) This president was one of the first to use the radio for broadcasting, specifically for regular monthly radio programs and to deliver a State of the Union address in 1923.
DefM: (1928) International agreement where the signing nations promised to renounce war and settle all disputes peacefully. Also carved an exception for "self-defense." Obviously failed with the start of WW2.

Name: Herbert Hoover
fact: This president attempted to stop the New Deal, specifically by pressuring the next president into renouncing key tenets of the New Deal, including deficit spending and public works programs.
DefE: (10/29/1929) the day that the New York Stock Exchange crashed, marking the start of the Great Depression (though not the sole cause of it).
DefM: (1932) Independent U.S. government agency created by this president's administration to provide emergency financial relief and loans to struggling banks, railroad, insurance companies, and agricultural institutions. Its powers expanded with the New Deal, and shifted in WWII to finance war production. Was abolished in 1957.

Name: Franklin D. Roosevelt
fact: This president contracted polio, but his team actively concealed his paralysis from the public. He was also discontent with his conservative Supreme Court, such that he wanted to expand the Court from 9 to 15 justices in a "court-packing" plan.
DefE: (1941) Critical turning point in U.S. when Japan attacked the U.S. Pacific Fleet stationed at Pearl Harbor, Hawaii. Killed over 2400 Americans, wounded more than 1000, and led to the U.S. joining WWII. It was also fueled by U.S. oil embargo after Japan invaded China (1937) and French Indochina (1940).
DefM: (1930s) Based on the three "R's": Relief, Recovery. and Reform. Included the extensive use of deficit spending, despite this president advocating for balancing the budget.

Name: Harry S. Truman
fact: This president is known for desegregating the the U.S. Armed Forces through issuing Executive Order 9981.
DefE: (1945) Surrender of Japan that ended WWII. This followed the atomic bombings on Hiroshima and Nagasaki, as well as the Soviet Union declaring war on Japan and invading Manchuria.
DefM: (1940s) An expansion of the New Deal, increased government support for social and economic welfare. Established the FEPC, passed anti-lynching legislation and abolished poll taxes. It also repealed the Taft-Hartley Act and raised the minimum wage, among other things.

Name: Dwight D. Eisenhower
fact: Following Brown v. Board of Education, this president sent federal troops to Little Rock, Arkansas, to enforce school desegregation, which included the escorting of the Little Rock Nine.
DefE: (1956) An international military and diplomatic conflict in Egypt that proved European imperial powers were no longer dominant and established the United States and the Soviet Union as the leading global superpowers.
DefM: (1954) Declared racial segregation at schools unconstitutional (unanimous 9-0); overturned 1896 Plessy v. Ferguson.

Name: John F. Kennedy
fact: He is the first Roman Catholic President and the first to receive a Pulitzer Prize or Purple Heart.
event: Bay of Pigs Invasion / Cuban Missile Crisis
DefE: (1961) Failed military invasion of Cuba by U.S.-backed Cuban exiles to overthrow Fidel Castro. This failure pushed Cuba even closer to the Soviet Union, leading to the Cuban Missile Crisis.
DefM: (1961) An independent agency of the United States federal government that sends American volunteers to work in developing nations on grassroots projects and cultural exchange.

Name: Lyndon B. Johnson
fact: This president received the Silver Star for serving in the Navy during WWII.
DefE: (1964) A congressional action that gave U.S. President Lyndon B. Johnson broad authority to wage military operations in Southeast Asia without a formal declaration of war. Served as justification for policies made during the Vietnam War.
DefM: (1960s) Included the War on Poverty, expansion of Healthcare, Civil Rights (like the act in 1964), Education Reform, Immigration policies, and Urban Housing policies, among others.

Name: Richard Nixon
fact: Though an anti-communist, this president is known for being the first U.S. president to visit the People's Republic of China in order to pursue detente.
event: Pentagon Papers, Watergate Scandal, Credibility Gap
DefE: (1970s) A top-secret 7,000-page Department of Defense study detailing the history of U.S. political and military involvement in Vietnam from 1945 to 1967. Revealed that administrations lied to the public and Congress about the scope of the U.S. involvement, plans, and likelihood of winning the Vietnam War.
DefM: (1969) Policy to end American combat involvement in the Vietnam War by transferring responsibilities to South Vietnam; led to the Fall of Saigon in 1975.

Name: Gerald Ford
fact: This president was never on the ballot, and was appointed vice president (due to the 25th amendment) after the last one had resigned.
DefE: (1975) Capture of South Vietnam's capital by North Vietnamese communist forces, ending the Vietnam War. United Vietnam under communist rule, and led to hundreds of thousands of refugees fleeing the country.
DefM: (1974) Pardon by this president for Richard Nixon.

Name: Jimmy Carter
fact: Post-presidency, this president went on to contribute humanitarian work, promoting human rights and public health, such that he would win a Nobel Peace Prize.
DefE: (1979-81) Diplomatic standoff where Iranian militants seized 52 American citizens at the U.S. Embassy in Tehran; the 1980 Operation Eagle Claw to rescue failed; only ended minutes after Reagan's inauguration following the signing of the Algiers Accords to unfreeze Iranian assets in exchange for the hostages' freedoms.
DefM: Signed on September 17, 1978, at the presidential retreat in Maryland, mediated by U.S. President Jimmy Carter between Egyptian President Anwar Sadat and Israeli Prime Minister Menachem Begin. Israel agreed to withdraw troops from Egypt, while Egypt recognized Israel; opened the Suez Canal and Red Sea to Israeli shipping.

Name: Ronald Reagan
fact: As a Hollywood actor, he appeared in over 50 films and was president of the Screen Actors Guild, where he fought against communism in the film industry and eventually shifted from Democrat to Republican.
DefE: (1983) Proposal for U.S. defense missile system relying on ground-based lasers, particle beams, and satellites to intercept Soviet nuclear missiles.
DefM: (1980s) Economic program to spur growth by tax cuts, deregulation, and reduced social spending rather than government-driven demand.

Name: George H.W. Bush
fact: This president once said "Read my lips: no new taxes." 2 years later, he agreed to a budget compromise with Congress that included tax increases to control deficits.
event: Fall of Berlin Wall / End of Soviet Union
act: Acquittal of Officers Who Beat Rodney King
DefE: (1989) Turning point in Cold War, symbolizing the collapse of Soviet hegemony in Eastern Europe and leading to German reunification in 1990 and the dissolution of the Soviet Union in 1991.
DefM: (1992) Acquittal of 4 LAPD officers who were videotaped beating up African American Rodney King. Ignited the 1992 Los Angeles Riots.

Name: Bill Clinton
fact: This president's wife went on to run for president, being the first (and only) FLOTUS to run for president.
DefE: (1990s) Political controversies involving this president's administration. Whitewater involved an investigation into a failed real estate venture, and Lewinsky involved a sex scandal where intern Monica Lewinsky was involved in a sexual relationship with this president. This president lied under oath, and was impeached, though remained in office.
DefM: (1996) Changed how the government provides financial assistance to low-income families.

Name: George W. Bush
fact: This president's policies and slow decisions during the recovery of Hurricane Katrina infamously led to rapper Kanye West claiming that this president "does not care about black people."
DefE: (2000s) Two devastating events that tested the Bush administration, with varying results. 9/11 garnered the Bush administration high support and launched the War on Terror, while also creating questions around American security. Hurricane Katrina gathered more polarization, mainly due to the slow disaster response and the disparities with how New Orleans, a city that is predominantly black, was left vulnerable.
DefM: (2001) Enacted after 9/11; expanded surveillance powers and especially wiretaps, among other things. It created the debate of national security vs. civil liberties in the wake of 9/11.

Name: Barack Obama
fact: This president's calm demeanor and frustrations lead to the creation of the character of this president's "anger translator."
DefE: (2015) Iran agreed to limit its nuclear program in exchange for relief from international economic and oil sanctions.
DefM: (2010) Healthcare reform act; required Americans to carry health insurance or pay a tax penalty; overall a large expansion of government involvement in healthcare. Zero Republican votes were made for this act, symbolizing the polarization of parties. It also sparked the Tea Party movement and Republican gains in 2010 midterms.

Name: Donald Trump
fact: This president once campaigned to free rapper A$AP Rocky when he was detained in Sweden.
DefE: (2021) Assault by crowd of Trump supporters on the U.S. Capitol to disrupt the security of Joe Biden's victory in the 2020 presidential election. Led to Trump's second impeachment by the House.
DefM: (2017) Federal law that lowered income tax rates for individuals and corporations.

Name: Joe Biden
fact: He became one of the youngest U.S. senators at 29 years old.
event: Withdrawl of American Troops from Afghanistan / Fall of Kabul
DefE: (2021) U.S. military end war in Afghanistan by withdrawing troops, which came 15 days after the Taliban captured Kabul. This followed a signed peace agreement by the U.S. and the Taliban in early 2020, where the U.S. agreed to pull out all troops.
DefM: (2021) $1.9 trillion economic stimulus package signed by Joe Biden to speed up U.S. recovery from COVID-19 pandemic.
